parts.text:
Build a clean, responsive ecommerce checkout page using React functional components and CSS.

Requirements:

1. Fetch the product catalogue from GET [http://localhost:8080/api/products](http://localhost:8080/api/products).
2. Let users add products to the cart and increase or decrease quantities.
3. Display product names, unit prices, quantities, and line totals.
4. Provide a coupon input with an Apply Coupon button and a Remove Coupon option.
5. Send cart product IDs, quantities, and couponCode to POST [http://localhost:8080/api/checkout](http://localhost:8080/api/checkout).
6. Display subtotal, discount, and final total using the backend response. Do not independently calculate the authoritative checkout total.
7. Display loading states, network errors, and coupon validation errors.
8. Prevent duplicate submissions while a checkout request is in progress.
9. Format displayed amounts as INR using Intl.NumberFormat.
10. Use accessible form labels, semantic HTML, and responsive CSS.
Keep components small and readable. Do not introduce unnecessary libraries. Explain the files you create and how to run the application.

# React + Vite

This template provides a minimal setup to get React working in Vite with HMR and some ESLint rules.

Currently, two official plugins are available:

- [@vitejs/plugin-react](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react) uses [Oxc](https://oxc.rs)
- [@vitejs/plugin-react-swc](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react-swc) uses [SWC](https://swc.rs/)

## React Compiler

The React Compiler is not enabled on this template because of its impact on dev & build performances. To add it, see [this documentation](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler/installation).

## Expanding the ESLint configuration

If you are developing a production application, we recommend using TypeScript with type-aware lint rules enabled. Check out the [TS template](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/tree/main/packages/create-vite/template-react-ts) for information on how to integrate TypeScript and [`typescript-eslint`](https://typescript-eslint.io) in your project.

# Checkout API

The Go API uses only the standard library and listens on port `8088` by default.
Run the following commands from the repository root:

```powershell
cd backend
go run .
```

In another terminal, run the backend tests from `backend/`:

```powershell
go test ./...
```

Set `PORT` to use a different listening port, for example `$env:PORT = "8090"`
in PowerShell before running `go run .`.

## Endpoints

- `GET /api/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.
- `GET /api/products` returns the server's product catalog. Prices are
  `pricePaise` integer values; `100` paise equals ₹1.
- `POST /api/checkout` accepts JSON in this shape:

  ```json
  {
    "items": [
      { "productId": "notebook", "quantity": 1 }
    ],
    "couponCode": "SAVE10"
  }
  ```

  `couponCode` is optional. The server looks up product prices itself, so
  checkout requests must not include client-supplied prices or totals.

Checkout responses contain `subtotalPaise`, `discountPaise`, and `totalPaise`.
`SAVE10` takes 10% off and rounds the discount down to a whole paise.
`FLAT100` takes ₹100 off, capped at the subtotal so the total cannot be
negative. An invalid coupon returns HTTP `400` with a JSON `error` field.

Checkout requests must use `Content-Type: application/json`. Request bodies are
limited to 1 MiB; carts are limited to 50 lines, 99 units per line, and 500 units
overall. The API allows browser requests from Vite's `http://localhost:5173`
and `http://127.0.0.1:5173` origins.

# Fieldnotes checkout

A responsive React storefront and checkout page for the checkout API. It loads
the product catalogue from `http://localhost:8088/api/products`, keeps cart
quantities in the browser, and asks the backend to validate coupons and
calculate checkout totals.

## Run locally

Start the API from the repository's `backend` directory, using port `8088`:

```powershell
$env:PORT = "8088"
go run .
```

In another terminal, start the frontend from this directory:

```powershell
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the local URL printed by Vite (normally `http://localhost:5173`). The
backend allows requests from that development origin. To verify the frontend
build and lint rules, run `npm run build` and `npm run lint`.

## Main files

- `src/App.jsx` contains the catalogue, cart, coupon flow, and backend checkout
  requests.
- `src/App.css` contains the storefront layout and responsive component styles.
- `src/index.css` contains global resets and base typography.
- `index.html` sets the browser page title and application entry point.
